text:
incident-bot: PAGER: continuous-batch throughput cliff detected in us-west-2 - elevated 5xx and request queueing. Auto-page sent to oncall-sam and sre rotation.

oncall-sam: got it, looking now. seeing spike in queue length on cb-pool-12.

sre-jen: confirming, we have sustained latency + token emission stalls. KV cache eviction rate spiked ~18x over baseline.

runtime-miguel: KV churn looks like a storm — lots of small request prefixes are blowing out the small shard caches. microbatch sizes jumping from 8->64 during bursts.

eng-kyla: are these mostly hosted-api customers or dedicated? any customer-facing errors?

cs-maya: Customer ops: several hosted customers in us-west-2 report interleaved timeouts, intermittent partial responses. One account saw 20% error rate on embeddings route.

telemetry-bot: metrics snapshot: 
- cb_queue_length_p50: 120 -> 1800
- kv_evictions/s: 5 -> 95
- inflight_microbatch_size_p95: 64
- 5xx_rate_hosted_us-west-2: 0.02 -> 0.18
(links: https://telemetry/redwood/alerts/1779003333)

oncall-sam: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle prefetch/prefill, 2) force microbatch cap to low value, 3) throttle KV eviction via config. Which is fastest?

runtime-miguel: fastest is forcing microbatch cap & disabling continuous jitter aggregation. patch config on the runtime layer, no model restart.

eng-kyla: do we have a safe config? recommend reducing max_microbatch to 4 and cb.max_inflight to 300 for this pool. Also enable cb.jitter_dampening=true.

sre-jen: agreed. prepare hotfix and roll canary to 1 node in pool then widen.

oncall-sam: I'll run the canary patch. tagging @runtime-miguel for rollback hook.

runtime-miguel: ready. rollout steps: 
1) curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/runtime/configs/apply -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"pool":"cb-pool-12","changes":{"cb.max_microbatch":4,"cb.max_inflight":300,"cb.jitter_dampening":true}}'
2) watch telemetry link above for queue length and 5xx.
3) if 5xx or latency worsens, revert with same endpoint ({"revert_to":"previous"}).

oncall-sam: executing step 1 canary now.

incident-bot: SYSTEM: canary rollout started (cb-pool-12, node cb-12-3).

oncall-sam: canary applied. initial tail latency dropping on node cb-12-3. kv_evictions on that node down 70%.

telemetry-bot: after canary (t+2m): cluster-level kv_evictions/s: 95 -> 62; cb_queue_length_p95: 1800 -> 950; 5xx_rate_us-west-2: 0.18 -> 0.11.

sre-jen: good signal. widening to 30% of pool.

runtime-miguel: widening... applying patch to remaining nodes gradually. watch for microburst where inflight drops and backlog shifts.

eng-kyla: also pushing a temporary throttle on prefetch: pf.backpressure=true for that pool. command:

```
POST /admin/prefetch/controls
{ "pool": "cb-pool-12", "prefetch_enabled": false, "backpressure_mode": "aggressive" }
```

cs-maya: customer ops reporting fewer timeouts already for the affected accounts. One enterprise reported partial outputs but no full failures now.

telemetry-bot: t+8m metrics: kv_evictions/s: 95 -> 22; cb_queue_length_p95: 1800 -> 320; 5xx_rate: 0.18 -> 0.04.

oncall-sam: looks stable. moving to mitigation->stabilization. documenting incident: early root cause hypothesis = KV cache thrash due to high-concurrency microbursts + continuous-batching jitter that inflated microbatch aggregation, which caused large variable microbatch sizes and cache pressure.

eng-kyla: followups: 
- short term (0-24h): promote hotfix cluster-wide for us-west-2, keep prefetch throttle until we validate.
- medium (24-72h): tune continuous-batching heuristics: add adaptive jitter dampening and cap microbatch growth per-second.
- long term: improve KV shard autosizing and backpressure to reduce eviction cascades.

product-lin: flagging customer impact for SRE postmortem and CS outreach. recommend notifying top affected customers with ETA for root-cause and mitigation summary.

cs-maya: we'll prepare a customer-facing note. would like exact timeline and impact numbers for their SLA review.

sre-jen: taking over for stabilization and post-incident. oncall-sam handing off. notes: 
- timestamp root: 1779003333
- actions taken: canary patch (max_microbatch=4, max_inflight=300, jitter_dampening=true), prefetch backpressure enabled.
- observed improvement window: 2-10 minutes after canary.

oncall-sam: handing off to sre-jen. I'm available if rollback needed. 

incident-bot: NOTE: created incident ticket INC-1779003333, assigned to SRE. Classified as Sev2: partial degradation of hosted API in us-west-2.

sre-jen: I'll schedule a postmortem and own the RCA. next steps: collect KV eviction traces, sampling of microbatch sizes per-request, and correlate with client sampling keys. Also validate no regression in tail latency for other regions.

runtime-miguel: I'll prepare a PR for the adaptive-jitter dampening heuristic and a smaller default max_microbatch for high-concurrency pools.

eng-kyla: add unit tests for eviction-rate simulation.

product-lin: CS will wait for final RCA before outreach.

sre-jen: closing incident channel for live mitigation. created followup task: SRE-1779003333-postmortem.

oncall-sam: thanks team, glad we caught it quickly. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: SYSTEM: Incident marked mitigated (mitigation timestamp: 1779004899).

sre-jen: postmortem owners: sre-jen, runtime-miguel, eng-kyla, cs-maya. I'll send meeting invite.

oncall-sam: handoff complete.
